_note: English texts for everything the API sends as a key. The long clinical texts (description, physiology, protocols, general advice) are DRAFTS to be validated by the clinical team. The short advice sentences of findings[].advice come in English from the backend.

heart.label: Cardiovascular
general: Keep well hydrated and watch sodium intake.
Complete the scheduled aerobic and resistive exercise sessions (ARED).
Measure blood pressure at rest, with the arm at heart level, and repeat it if it is abnormal.
Watch for dizziness on standing, chest pain or palpitations and tell the flight surgeon if they appear.
Update the personal baseline for heart rate and blood pressure.
heart.description: Heart and blood pressure: weightlessness redistributes fluids and puts a load on the cardiovascular system.
heart.physiology: In microgravity blood moves toward the upper body and the heart works under a different load. Heart rate, pressure and heart rate variability are compared with the pre-flight baseline.

lungs.label: Respiratory
general: Check that ventilation is not blocked and that the CO₂ scrubbers are working.
Reduce physical effort in the module if there is headache or fatigue.
Ask for slow, deep breaths and repeat the saturation reading.
Check the sensor placement before reading a low saturation.
Report shortness of breath, dizziness or bluish lips.
lungs.description: Oxygenation, breathing and cabin air quality.
lungs.physiology: In a closed environment CO₂ builds up easily. An alert is raised from 2.3 mmHg and 3.0 mmHg is the limit; headache usually appears before reaching it.

brain.label: Central nervous system / Brain
general: Protect the 8.5 h sleep block: avoid bright light and pending tasks before bed.
Control noise and temperature in the sleeping module.
Repeat the PVT test every 4 days and compare it with the hours of sleep.
Keep in touch with the crew and with psychological support on Earth.
Repeat the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 questionnaires on schedule and review the workload.
brain.description: Sleep, cognitive performance and behavioral health (PHQ-9 and GAD-7 questionnaires).
brain.hardware: Actiwatch actigraph + PVT-B test + digital psychometric questionnaires
brain.physiology: Little sleep slows reflexes (PVT-B test) and raises stress. Isolation and confinement also weigh on mood, so the questionnaires are repeated and Item 9 of the PHQ-9 is watched.

metabolism.label: Endocrine / Metabolism
general: Follow the eating and hydration plan given by the flight surgeon.
Record glucose with its context (fasting or after eating) so it can be interpreted.
Keep fast carbohydrates (15 g) at hand in case glucose drops.
Repeat the measurement if the value is out of range before acting.
Report intense thirst, trembling, cold sweat or confusion.
metabolism.physiology: Stress, the flight diet and exercise change how glucose is handled. The reading is interpreted in context: fasting or after eating.

thermal.label: Thermoregulation / Immunity
general: Hydrate and check the ventilation and temperature of the module.
Remove layers of clothing or increase local ventilation if the temperature is high.
After exercise, cool down gradually and measure again after 15 minutes.
Look for symptoms of infection or heat exhaustion.
Tell the flight surgeon if the temperature does not drop after 30 minutes of rest.
thermal.physiology: Without natural convection the body loses heat poorly. A sustained rise in temperature can point to infection or heat fatigue, and it has to be judged against the activity.

radiation.label: Whole body / Radiation
general: Stay in shielded areas during solar particle events.
Check the dosimeters and review the time spent in poorly shielded areas.
Postpone non-essential spacewalks (EVA) if the radiation rate rises.
Note the accumulated dose and any symptom (nausea, dizziness) in the medical record.
Plan future exposures according to the career limit.
radiation.description: Radiation dose received and the career dose against its limit.
radiation.physiology: Outside the protection of Earth the dose builds up. The daily rate, the percentage of the agency's career limit and solar particle events are watched.

bones.label: Bone and muscle
general: Complete the scheduled resistive exercise sessions (ARED).
Make sure calcium and vitamin D intake is as indicated by the flight surgeon.
Schedule the bone density scans (DXA) and compare their evolution with the pre-flight baseline.
Report bone, back or joint pain that does not go away.
Combine resistive and aerobic exercise: without load, bone is lost continuously.
bones.description: Bone density and adherence to resistive exercise.
bones.physiology: Without mechanical load bone is lost continuously. Resistive exercise (ARED) is the main countermeasure.

eyes.label: Eyes (SANS)
general: Report blurred vision, changes in sharpness or persistent headaches right away (possible SANS).
Do the scheduled eye checks (visual acuity and OCT).
Watch blood pressure and cabin CO₂, which influence intracranial pressure.
Rest your eyes and avoid bright light before sleeping.
Note any change in vision with its date and duration.
eyes.description: Head and vision symptoms linked to spaceflight associated neuro-ocular syndrome.
eyes.hardware: Ocular tomography (OCT, on Earth) + crew reports
eyes.physiology: The shift of fluids toward the head can change the eye. Reports of headache or blurred vision are followed closely.

protocols.green: No action required. Continue with the mission routine.
protocols.yellow: Watch the indicator and repeat the measurement as recommended.
protocols.orange: Priority attention: follow the recommendation, reduce the workload and notify the flight surgeon.
protocols.red: Emergency: apply the immediate action and contact the flight surgeon now.
